uncited: Gradient estimation and smoothing techniques address discontinuities in differentiable rendering that cause vanishing gradients.

This family modifies gradient computation by smoothing the integrand to permit differentiation under the integral sign, approximating gradients via non-local spatial statistics, or applying axis-aligned filters [6449-smooth-gradient-estimation-via-convolution.md, 6784-non-local-approximated-gradients.md, 7600-axis-aligned-neighbor-smoothing.md].

Methods in this family either smooth the rendering integrand via convolution to allow Leibniz's rule to exchange differentiation and integration, or approximate gradients using differential filters on rendered images to propagate gradients beyond immediate primitive boundaries [6449-smooth-gradient-estimation-via-convolution.md, 6784-non-local-approximated-gradients.md].
Both aim to provide non-zero, directed gradients that guide optimization away from local minima [6449-smooth-gradient-estimation-via-convolution.md, 6784-non-local-approximated-gradients.md].
